A features-and-fixes release. Cloud sessions can now be sent to, stopped, archived and deleted from Buddy; New chat can start Codex and Grok sessions under any of your accounts; a far machine's agent team draws every member, linked to its lead; and Windows gets a round of fixes, most visibly badges that render properly instead of as colour emoji.

## New

- **Talk to a Claude Code cloud session from its chat panel.** Send messages into a running cloud session and stop it, from the same panel you already use for local sessions. A live cloud session's panel also has its browser link back.
- **Archive or delete a cloud session** from its orb's right-click menu.
- **Cloud orbs for every account.** Buddy reads every Claude Code account you're signed into for cloud sessions, and sends with the login that owns each one. A login under a custom config directory is found, and a blanked login reads as signed out instead of as an error.
- **New chat can start Codex and Grok sessions under a chosen account**, not only Claude Code ones.
- **A far machine's agent team draws every member.** When both machines run Buddy and are linked directly, each team member gets its own smaller orb, with its own initials and colour and an arrow to its lead — the same as a team on this machine. A machine without Buddy still shows nothing.
- **Usage orbs have their own switch and hotkey**, separate from the session orbs.
- **Separate Speech and Alert volume sliders**, and a button that previews a Speak voice from the settings window.

## Fixed

- **Windows badges and button marks are drawn, not turned into colour emoji.** Windows was replacing several symbols with emoji, which looked wrong and ignored the orb's colours.
- **Only one Buddy per user on macOS.** Starting Buddy from a second login session no longer gives you two copies, and installing a new build no longer leaves the old one running beside it.
- **Buddy stays responsive with many sessions open.** Reading what is under each session, agent-team membership and turning on file watchers all moved off the UI thread; with many sessions these could freeze the orbs for seconds at a time.
- **A turn's sound no longer plays twice** when two turns finish close together.
- **Speech says "Spend limit reached"** instead of "Summary unavailable" when that's the reason, and the summariser passes its instruction as an argument rather than on stdin.
- **New chat under a named account starts with that account's login** on the first try.
- **Windows text-to-speech handles any text and voice name**, including quotes and non-ASCII characters.
- **Windows file properties show the real version number**, and the installer's PowerShell scripts run under Windows PowerShell 5.1 as well as PowerShell 7.
- The Remote Control panel no longer refers to the old relay, which was removed in an earlier release.

Behind the scenes, a long list of intermittent test failures on both platforms were traced to their real causes and fixed, and the coverage tooling now measures every suite on Windows and refuses to report a number it didn't actually measure.

## Known limitations

- A far machine's agent team is drawn only when that machine also runs Buddy and is linked directly.
- A per-user Windows install adds no firewall rule for the peer link, because that needs admin rights. Windows asks the first time Buddy listens.

| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.10-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |

## Upgrading

Replace the app as usual. **On macOS, if you re-install you have to re-grant the Automation and Local Network permissions.** Replacing `/Applications/Claude Buddy.app` gives the app a new code identity, and macOS doesn't carry those permissions over to it. Without Automation, click-to-focus stops working; without Local Network, anything on your LAN, such as an OpenClaw gateway or a remote-control peer, can't be reached. Re-grant both in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
